# docker_network (Resource)

A Docker network (`NetworkCreate`): a local `bridge`/`macvlan`/`ipvlan` network, or a Swarm-scoped `overlay` network when the daemon is a Swarm manager. Docker networks cannot be changed after creation, so every argument forces a new network. Import by network name or ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A user-defined bridge network with a static subnet.
resource "docker_network" "app" {
  name   = "app"
  labels = { team = "web" }

  ipam_config {
    subnet  = "10.20.0.0/24"
    gateway = "10.20.0.1"
  }
}

# A Swarm overlay network standalone containers may also join
# (requires the daemon to be a Swarm manager).
resource "docker_network" "mesh" {
  name       = "mesh"
  driver     = "overlay"
  attachable = true
}

# A swarm-scoped macvlan network: each node holds a config-only network with
# its local parent interface and subnet, and the swarm network takes its
# configuration from it (docker network create --config-only / --config-from).
resource "docker_network" "macvlan_config" {
  name        = "macvlan-config"
  driver      = "macvlan"
  config_only = true
  options     = { parent = "eth0" }

  ipam_config {
    subnet = "192.168.50.0/24"
  }
}

resource "docker_network" "macvlan" {
  name        = "macvlan"
  driver      = "macvlan"
  scope       = "swarm"
  config_from = docker_network.macvlan_config.name
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Network name. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `adopt` (Boolean) Take over an object whose `io.terraform.provider.owner` label names a different owner than the provider's `owner` argument (for example after `terraform import`). Without it, planning such an object fails. Only checked when the provider sets `owner`. Default `false`.
- `attachable` (Boolean) Let standalone containers attach to an `overlay` network. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `config_from` (String) Name of the config-only network that provides this network's configuration (`ConfigFrom.Network`), e.g. for a swarm-scoped `macvlan` network. The network takes its IPAM, IPv4/IPv6 settings and labels from it: `labels`, `ipam_config`, `ipam_options`, `enable_ipv4 = false` and `enable_ipv6 = true` are rejected with it (the Engine refuses them), and no owner or managed-by label is added. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `config_only` (Boolean) Create a config-only network (`ConfigOnly`): a placeholder holding IPAM and driver options for other networks' `config_from`; containers cannot attach to it. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `driver` (String) Network driver: `bridge` (default), `overlay` (Swarm manager only), `macvlan`, `ipvlan`, or a plugin. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `enable_ipv4` (Boolean) Enable IPv4 on the network (`EnableIPv4`); `false` disables IPv4 IPAM (only for networks that support it). Unset uses the daemon default (enabled), which is not reported. Changing this forces a new resource. Needs Engine API >= 1.48.
- `enable_ipv6` (Boolean) Enable IPv6 on the network (`EnableIPv6`). Changing this forces a new resource.
- `ingress` (Boolean) Create the Swarm routing-mesh (ingress) network. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `internal` (Boolean) Restrict external access to the network. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `ipam_config` (Block List) Static IPAM pools. Without this block the daemon assigns a subnet itself (not reported in state). Forces replacement when a configured value differs from the network's: a missing block, or an argument left unset in a pool, accepts what the network already has (e.g. the daemon-assigned pool a kreuzwerker/docker state records) and only drops it from state. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--ipam_config))
- `ipam_driver` (String) IPAM driver. Default `default`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `ipam_options` (Map of String) IPAM driver options (`IPAM.Options`), e.g. for a third-party IPAM plugin. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `labels` (Map of String) Network labels. Docker has no network update, so changing this forces a new resource.
- `options` (Map of String) Driver options, e.g. `{ "com.docker.network.bridge.name" = "br-app" }`. Options the driver adds itself are not reported. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `scope` (String) Level at which the network exists (`Scope`): `local` (this host) or `swarm` (cluster-wide; `global` is also accepted by plugins). Unset lets the driver decide, and the daemon's value is reported. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `content_sha256` (String) sha256 of inspect_json.
- `docker_server_version` (String) Docker Engine version from GET /version.
- `engine_api_version` (String) Engine API version negotiated with the daemon (min of the client maximum and GET /version ApiVersion).
- `id` (String) Network ID.
- `inspect` (Attributes) The GET /networks/{id} response as a nested object, field by field. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--inspect))
- `inspect_json` (String) The exact Engine API GET /networks/{id} response as JSON.

<a id="nestedblock--ipam_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ipam_config`

Optional:

- `aux_address` (Map of String) Auxiliary addresses the IPAM driver must not hand out, name to IP.
- `gateway` (String) Gateway address. Unset lets the daemon pick (not reported).
- `ip_range` (String) Sub-range to allocate container IPs from.
- `subnet` (String) Subnet in CIDR form, e.g. `10.20.0.0/24`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by network name or ID.
terraform import docker_network.app app
```
